issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a method named swiftExperienceDescription() on Developer and instruct calling it from the initializer, but the solution implements and uses a differently named method getExperienceDescription(). This name/signature mismatch between solution and problem/template can confuse students comparing implementations or referencing the example solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution consistent with the specification and template by renaming getExperienceDescription() to swiftExperienceDescription() and update calls accordingly (or, alternatively, update the problem statement and template to use getExperienceDescription()). Ensure the initializer calls the same method name as documented in the problem statement.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template require a Developer instance method named swiftExperienceDescription(), but the solution implementation uses getExperienceDescription() instead. This names the same conceptual operation (producing a printable Swift-experience description) with two different identifiers across artifacts, causing students to be unsure which method name to implement or call. The inconsistency also appears in initializer and client call sites (initializer in solution calls getExperienceDescription(), while the client code calls swiftExperienceDescription()), which creates additional confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across all artifacts. Rename the solution's getExperienceDescription() to swiftExperienceDescription() and update any calls in the solution (initializer and Client) to call swiftExperienceDescription(), so the template, problem statement, and solution consistently use the same identifier.
